instruction: First use ONLY the physical left R5 arm to grasp the tennis ball on the black support, lift it a small visible distance and verify retention. Keep the physical right arm at its current pose during this stage. Only after the ball is visibly lifted and retained, hold the left arm and use the physical right R5 arm to grasp and slightly lift the red cola can. The operator specifically requests lower finger contact height before closing. Finish holding both objects; do not home or release.
content: Current scene supersedes every older screen-direction hint: the external camera has moved to the opposite side. In the current global image the physical left arm and tennis ball are on SCREEN RIGHT, and the physical right arm and red cola can are on SCREEN LEFT. Physical identities remain left=can0=left wrist image and right=can1=right wrist image. The image named top is an oblique elevated RGB view, not a calibrated overhead view. Each arm has its own base axes; do not infer metric coordinates or signs from screen axes.

Execute sequentially. During tennis approach, closure and verified lift, every motion and gripper action must set the right side to null. After fresh images establish that the tennis ball left its support and remains retained, hold left with null and proceed on right. The host opens the empty jaws before inference. No previous run has demonstrated a successful grasp in this setup.

Lesson from failed grasps: wrist centering and an object projected between finger tips did not mean enclosure. The fingers often remained above or in front of the objects. With open jaws, align the INNER CONTACT SURFACES with the ball equator or can body, and achieve sufficient insertion depth before closing. Prefer lower contact on the object body, not an overhead pinch. The black support, tabletop, can rim, cables and the other arm must remain clear. Lowering does not mean pressing into the support or table. Use both the shared global view and selected wrist view to disambiguate height and forward distance.

Recent lowering failures: preserving reset wrist orientation while blindly decreasing TCP Z produced official IK branch refusals and poorly tracked negative J3 targets. This is a planning/tracking clue, not a proven hardware joint limit. Do not replay a rejected descent or keep forcing negative J3. Reassess reachable wrist pitch and forward reach, and use check_path for a modest posture adjustment if appropriate. Choose bounded, visually supported corrections and inspect actual J1..J6 and executed TCP response. A successful numerical plan alone does not certify clearance.

Keep decisions concise. Use move_to or short move_eef_chunk with fresh observations and original GPT-Policy Cartesian tools. A planning rejection is not an executed move. Keep existing trajectory, residual and freshness checks. Do not increase motion after a tracking fault or interpret it as contact. Do not replay old absolute poses after a reset or release.

Close only the ready side after corroborated placement. Gripper raw/normalized positions are not force sensing and TCP offset is only an 8 cm estimate. Respect the reported gripper_next_opening_bounds. Confirm finger-object interaction, then make one small lift. Success requires the object to leave its support and remain retained in fresh global and wrist images. If it stays supported, the grasp failed: reopen, reassess height and insertion before another attempt. Do not repeat empty closures/lifts. done requires both objects visibly held.
